title: Tokamak Energy ST40
summary: A compact spherical tokamak using high-temperature superconducting magnets.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

Tokamak Energy's ST40 reached plasma temperatures above 100 million degrees in 2022, a necessary but far-from-sufficient condition for fusion. The company argues that spherical tokamaks with high-temperature superconducting magnets can be smaller and cheaper than ITER-class machines. It is now designing a pilot plant, with no demonstration of net energy gain yet.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Proof of concept
Estimated window 2022–2032
Confidence label Researching
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

Investment Exposure

Fusion's near-term investable edge is magnets and materials, not electricity; the plant is a long option.

What Would Change The View

  • Magnet field strength at scale.
  • Funding to the next machine.
  • Independent replication of temperature claims.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
